audit_kind: read-only implementation audit against the frozen spec
computation_performed: One 0.181-second DP fault-injection check on a single small family; no gate replay, full census, class-share calculation, child process, or substantial allocation.

conformant_checks.observation: Normalizes definitions, calls LS.usual, then uses exactly the specified TOP iteration and main relation.
conformant_checks.subject: Usual limit

conformant_checks.observation: Own distinctions are allocated before each body; non-self-holding callees are expanded depth first in body order, while self-holding calls retain their identity.
conformant_checks.subject: Inlining

conformant_checks.observation: S is selected from the first self-holding call, and entry/ray positions select the first or last corresponding calls as requested.
conformant_checks.subject: Ray selection

conformant_checks.observation: The initial image unions all incoming columns, so no incoming condition is imposed; W may contain any main distinction and must contain one of all k main ports.
conformant_checks.subject: Start block with k greater than three

conformant_checks.observation: Each forgotten table is compiled from W with that member removed, using its complete assignment table.
conformant_checks.subject: Full forgotten-member tables

conformant_checks.observation: Middle operations admit the empty subset; closing operations require a nonempty subset and the stated F/Gf acceptance test.
conformant_checks.subject: Middle and closing subsets

conformant_checks.observation: S1-S3 precede symbolic S4; S4 is evaluated before the block-size cap. Symbolic S4 follows the declared K/side/ray participation test.
conformant_checks.subject: Settled-class order

conformant_checks.observation: Capped graphs omit unknown transitions and are marked incomplete. Classification accepts incomplete graphs only with bounded_all or eventually_bounded true; otherwise they remain unresolved.
conformant_checks.subject: Incomplete graph and positive certificates

conformant_checks.observation: Default node, family time, and block-size limits match the frozen numbers. The memory exception is recorded separately above.
conformant_checks.subject: Declared graph and time caps

conformant_checks.observation: The ordinary task path uses at most N-1 children plus the computing parent. The distinct G1 startup exception is recorded above.
conformant_checks.subject: Ordinary census process accounting

conformant_checks.observation: One writer appends and fsyncs results and skips completed keys; duplicate existing keys are rejected. Interrupted-tail exceptions are recorded above.
conformant_checks.subject: Append ownership and duplicate keys

evidence.method: Wrap the original referee call, set a flag after it returns, and have rss_bytes report 3000000001 only after that flag.

core_findings.issue: The per-worker 3 GB stop is checked only by checkpoint. productive_and_cycles and the referee exact test have no checkpoint calls, and no checkpoint runs after the referee returns. A family may therefore finish as done above the worker memory ceiling.
core_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce per-worker RSS throughout every computed stage using an owned-process guard, and force a checkpoint after the referee calculation. Preserve the aggregate limit as a separate stop.

core_findings.issue: The full runner reads gate["passed"], but validation.run_gate1 returns gate_ok and no passed field. Both --only-gate664 and normal full-run startup raise KeyError after G1.
core_findings.suggested_fix: Use gate_ok consistently, or adapt the validator result once before inspecting it.

core_findings.issue: The pre-census G1 call passes workers=N to a validator that creates Pool(N), so N children run in addition to the runner parent. --workers 4 therefore has five processes despite the four-process ceiling and the runner parent-inclusive contract.
core_findings.suggested_fix: Make gate worker accounting parent-inclusive or use at most N-1 gate children when N>1. The single-worker path should remain in the parent.

core_findings.issue: Normal resume rejects a malformed final row instead of recovering its valid prefix. A valid final JSON object without a trailing newline is accepted, then the next append concatenates two objects on one line.
core_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve only the owned interrupted final tail and resume from the valid prefix. Add a newline before appending after a valid newline-less final object. Continue to reject malformed interior rows.

evidence.trigger: aggregate threshold crossed while the selected process is between guarded family calculations

core_findings.issue: The aggregate monitor can signal any alive child, including a child outside compute_family. It can also signal the parent after compute_family has restored the prior SIGUSR1 handler but before pending_parent is cleared. If that prior handler is SIG_DFL, the stop signal terminates the process instead of returning an unresolved family.
core_findings.status: conditional signal race at audited snapshot
core_findings.suggested_fix: Install a persistent safe idle SIGUSR1 handler for the invocation and make computation guard lifetimes explicit; avoid sending a stop signal outside a guarded computation.
